3. Data Sources

Observed Data

This pairing includes observed data from four different ocean time series: the Bermuda Atlantic Time-Series Study (BATS); the European Station for Time-Series in the Ocean, Canary Islands (ESTOC); the Carbon Retention In a Colored Ocean (CARIACO) Program; and the Hawaii Ocean Time-Series (HOT). Data from these stations have been used in numerous peer-reviewed publications; for example, Bates et al. (2014). These are the same sources featured in Figure 1 of EPA’s Ocean Acidity indicator.

Model Outputs

This pairing presents outputs from seven global climate models (GCMs) within the World Climate Research Programme (WCRP) Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) suite. While other pairings with GCM outputs use a standardized set of 16 GCMs, nine of those GCMs have not published results for this acidity variable, so this feature is based on the other seven GCMs from the set. Specific runs are noted in parentheses:

  • CanESM5 (r1i1p2f1)
  • GFDL-ESM4 (r1i1p1f1)
  • IPSL-CM6A-LR (r1i1p1f1)
  • MPI-ESM1-2-HR (r1i1p1f1)
  • MPI-ESM1-2-LR (r1i1p1f1)
  • NorESM2-LM (r1i1p1f1)
  • NorESM2-MM (r1i1p1f1)

Specifically, this analysis uses the “ph” variable, which represents sea water pH reported on a total scale. “Total scale” refers to the way pH is measured in this case, and it is consistent with high-quality analytical measurements such as those used for this pairing’s observed data. NCEI’s site provides a brief description and reference links regarding the different scales used to measure pH. GCMs can output pH for multiple depths in the water column. For this analysis, the project team chose the layer from each model that was closest to 2 meters depth. Available depths varied by model, so the resulting selections ranged from 0 to 6 meters.

4. Data Availability

Observed Data

Raw data from the four ocean sampling programs are publicly available online. In the case of Bermuda and the Canary Islands, updated data were procured directly from the scientists leading those programs. BATS data and descriptions are available from the Bermuda Institute of Ocean Sciences and Arizona State University BATS site. CARIACO data are provided by the Biological & Chemical Oceanography Data Management Office. ESTOC data can be downloaded from the Oceanic Platform of the Canary Islands (PLOCAN) site, although the ESTOC surface buoy stopped transmitting data after it was damaged in July 2010, and data access has been incomplete since then. HOT data were downloaded from the HOT Data Organization and Graphical System site. Additionally, annual HOT data reports are available online.

Model Outputs

CMIP6 monthly climate model outputs were retrieved from the publicly available CMIP6 data archive hosted by the Earth System Grid Federation. The overall technical documentation [to be linked] for this effort identifies the organizational ownership and direct source links for each of the individual models.
